idiom_name: exported method on a struct delegating to a hook interface or function field
implementation_notes: Go has neither subclasses nor virtual dispatch, so NVI becomes an explicit collaboration: the exported method on the outer type performs validation or instrumentation and calls a hook held as a named field - a small interface (Validator, Store) or a function value. Embedding a base struct is the wrong tool: the embedded method's receiver is resolved statically at compile time, so a promoted method calling b.Validate reaches the embedded Validate, never an outer implementation, and super-style extension does not exist. The Go FAQ and Effective Go recommend this composition model over type hierarchies; the interface call is dynamic and is exactly the extension point.
pitfalls: Embedding a base struct to imitate inheritance binds hook calls to the embedded receiver (static resolution, no virtual dispatch): the outer implementation never runs.
A nil interface in the hook field panics on call - validate or default it in the constructor and fail fast.
Promoted methods enlarge the outer type's method set, so unrelated interfaces are satisfied by accident; keep the dependency a named field and forward only what the API should expose.
